_comment: Curated A3 Pre-Regulator test points. Hand-authored from Table 4-3 (PDF p42,
manual p4-18) and the Battery Charger Adjustment Procedure §4-44 (PDF p38,
manual p4-14); the nets each point sits on were read off schematic 732A-1003
(Figure 8-3 cont., PDF p89) and are recorded in docs/review-notes.md and
docs/manual/08-schematic-and-interconnect-notes.md.
Table 4-3 prints one-sided limits for TP3 and TP2 (<=60V, <=31V) and bare
nominals for TP6 (32V) and TP5 (33.0V) with no tolerance. The bare nominals
carry an ASSUMED tolerance marked inferred: true -- +/-5 % on the 32 V
pre-regulator (the manual itself says 'approximately 32V dc', §3-11) and
+/-0.5 V on the 33.0 V trickle reference (printed to a tenth of a volt in
§4-44 step 10). Edit them in Author Mode if the shop uses different limits.
TP2 has no single correct reading: Table 4-3 gives <=31 V with the battery on
charge, and §4-44 steps 16-21 walk it through 45-50 V, ~26 V, 32 V, 24.5-26.5 V
and >31 V with W1 removed and a rheostat standing in for the battery. Each of
those is a state with its own setup text and citation.
All voltages are positive: every measured point is positive with respect to
its refPoint (Table 4-3 lists the positive point first; §4-44 steps 7 and 14
say so in words). TP1 (-BATTERY) and TP4 (-RAW) are the returns. On the sheet
the TP4 return line runs to P3-18 and the TP1 line to P3-17, and pins 17/18 are
drawn tied, so the two returns are one node at the connector (see the caveat
in a3.reference.json); they are kept apart here because Table 4-3 names them
separately and the trace between them carries the charge current.
Footnote to Table 4-3: measurements taken with Multimeter A (Table 4-1: 4-1/2
digit, 200 mV to 200 V, Fluke 8050A / 8060A).

testpoints.signal: RAW DC (bridge CR1 +, top of C1)
testpoints.condition: AC line power applied at the voltage marked on the rear panel; TP3 positive with respect to TP4. Multimeter A (Table 4-1).
testpoints.source: Table 4-3, PDF p42 (manual p4-18): 'A3 | TP3, TP4 | <=60V dc | AC line voltage, Rectifier, Power Transformer'
testpoints.note: Table 4-3 corrective action: AC line voltage (rear-panel setting, S1/S2 positions, F1), Rectifier (CR1), Power Transformer (T1 -- Table 4-2 sends a transformer fault back to Fluke). The raw dc before the pre-regulator; net traced on 732A-1003.

testpoints.source: Figure 8-3 (cont), 732A-1003, PDF p89; Table 4-3 lists TP4 as the low lead for TP3 and TP6
testpoints.note: Return for TP3 and TP6. Same line as P3-8 (-RAW) and P3-7 (AC POWER LED -). On the sheet this line also runs to P3-18, which is drawn tied to P3-17 (-BATTERY, TP1).

testpoints.signal: +RAW (pre-regulator output, Q1 emitter after R1, P3-2)
testpoints.condition: AC line power applied at the marked voltage; TP6 positive with respect to TP4. Multimeter A (Table 4-1).
testpoints.source: Table 4-3, PDF p42 (manual p4-18): 'A3 | TP6, TP4 | 32V dc | Pre-Regulator'; §3-4 and §3-11 (PDF p21) 'approximately 32V dc'; the A4 side of the same rail is Table 4-3 'A4 | TP1, TP3 | 32V dc'
testpoints.note: Table 4-3 gives no tolerance; +/-1.6 V (5 %) is assumed because §3-11 calls the value 'approximately 32V dc'. Q1 is an emitter follower whose base reference is set by the 30 V zener CR10 (through CR5) standing on the AC POWER LED node (R9 pull-up from TP3, CR12 5.2 V clamp, front-panel AC PWR LED across P3-4/7), fed by current-regulator diodes CR25/CR24 from the raw supply (traced on 732A-1003; see the caveat in a3.reference.json), so a wrong reading points at that chain as much as at Q1.

testpoints.signal: Charger output / battery-voltage sense (CR26-CR14 node, R11, W1 lower end, P3-11)
testpoints.source: Table 4-3, PDF p42 (manual p4-18) and §4-44 steps 16-21, PDF p38 (manual p4-14)
testpoints.note: With jumper W1 installed, TP2 is the charger output: the Q2 current-source collector line through W1 and CR13 to +BATTERY (P3-9/10). With W1 removed (§4-44 step 12) TP2 is only the charger's battery-voltage sense node, fed by current-regulator diode CR26 and loaded by the rheostat, so the rheostat stands in for the battery. Net traced on 732A-1003.

states.label: Normal: battery on charge (Table 4-3)
states.setup: Battery installed, BATTERY OPR switch ON (Table 4-3 note **), ac line power applied, W1 installed. TP2 positive with respect to TP1. Multimeter A.
states.source: Table 4-3, PDF p42: 'A3 | TP2, TP1 | <=31V dc | Battery Charger**'

states.label: §4-44 step 16: W1 removed, R10 fully CW, rheostat at maximum
states.setup: Jumper W1 removed (step 12), 50 kOhm rheostat between TP1 and TP2 at maximum resistance (step 6), BATTERY OPR ON (step 15), ac power through the Variac at the marked line voltage, R10 fully clockwise. Multimeter A between TP2 and TP1.
states.source: §4-44 step 16, PDF p38: 'Multimeter A should read approximately 45 to 50V dc.'
states.note: The manual says 'approximately'; the band is printed as 45 to 50 V.

states.label: §4-44 step 17: rheostat reduced until BTRY CHG comes on
states.setup: Continuing from step 16: adjust the rheostat toward minimum resistance while watching Multimeter A. At approximately 26 V dc the BTRY CHG indicator (and the on-board LED DS1, which the manual calls 'CR27') comes on and the ac line current jumps to approximately 110 mA at 115 V ac (55 mA at 220 V ac).
states.note: The manual prints 'approximately 26V dc' with no band; +/-1.5 V is assumed here, consistent with the 24.5 to 26.5 V band the same transition must meet in step 20.

states.label: §4-44 step 18: set with the rheostat
states.setup: Adjust the rheostat for a Multimeter A reading of 32 V dc, then (step 19) turn R10 counter-clockwise until the BTRY CHG indicator and DS1 ('CR27') go out and the ac line current drops.
states.note: This is the value you set the rheostat to, not a check; +/-0.5 V is assumed as the setting resolution. It is the threshold at which the high-rate charge must switch off (§3-28: 'When the battery voltage rises to approximately 32V, Q4 turns off').

states.label: §4-44 step 20: BTRY CHG lights again
states.setup: Adjust the rheostat toward minimum resistance while observing the BTRY CHG indicator. When it lights (DS1 lights too) and the ac line current increases suddenly, read Multimeter A.
states.source: §4-44 step 20, PDF p38: 'Multimeter A should read between 24.5 and 26.5V dc.'

states.label: §4-44 step 21: BTRY CHG goes out again
states.setup: Adjust the rheostat until the BTRY CHG and DS1 ('CR27') indicators turn off, then read Multimeter A.
states.source: §4-44 step 21, PDF p38: 'Multimeter A should indicate a dc voltage greater than +31V.'

testpoints.signal: Trickle-charge reference (Q6 base; CR28 / R16 / R17 / RT1 node)
testpoints.condition: Table 4-3: battery installed, BATTERY OPR switch ON, ac line power applied; TP5 positive with respect to TP1. §4-44 step 10 sets it with R20 under different conditions: W1 installed, BATTERY OPR OFF, 50 kOhm rheostat between TP1 and TP2 at maximum, ac power through the Variac at the marked line voltage. Multimeter A.
testpoints.source: Table 4-3, PDF p42 (manual p4-18): 'A3 | TP5, TP1 | 33.0V dc | Battery Charger**'; §4-44 step 10, PDF p38: 'Adjust R20 for a 33.0V dc reading on Multimeter A.'
testpoints.note: Set by R20 (§3-28: 'R20 sets this voltage level'). No tolerance is published; +/-0.5 V is assumed because the manual prints the value to a tenth of a volt. Errata Issue 3 (7/85) #12 adds a final check that supersedes the setting in practice: with a known-good battery pack in trickle mode the battery-charging voltage at the rear-panel connector must be 25.8 to 27 V, adjusting R20 if not (see procedure 4-44 step 27). Rev F boards (Errata Change #10) add R19 15 kOhm between R18 and R20 in this divider. A3 RT1, in parallel with R17 at this node, compensates the trickle voltage for ambient temperature (§3-28).

testpoints.signal: -BATTERY (P3-17/18; bottom of R14 / R20 / C5 / C6 / CR15)
testpoints.source: Figure 8-3 (cont), 732A-1003, PDF p89; Table 4-3 lists TP1 as the low lead for TP2 and TP5; §4-44 steps 6, 7 and 14
testpoints.note: Return for TP2 and TP5, and one end of the 50 kOhm rheostat in §4-44. Drawn tied to P3-18 at the connector, which is where the TP4 (-RAW) return line also arrives, so -BATTERY and -RAW are one node there (and on A4, whose TP3 sits on the shared -BATTERY / -RAW bus).
